evidence.quote: I mapped how a repair request moved between the reception desk and the volunteer fixing it. We were copying the same information into two notebooks. I drew the steps with the team, tried one shared form for a week and checked whether anything was missing. We kept the simpler process and wrote down who updates each field.
evidence.mark: mapped how a repair request moved between the reception desk and the volunteer fixing it

evidence.quote: I taught new volunteers how to record a repair and find the safety instructions. I made a short practice exercise, watched each person try it and changed the guide where they hesitated.
evidence.mark: taught new volunteers how to record a repair and find the safety instructions

evidence.quote: I monitored a community media server during live broadcasts. I recorded response times and disk usage, compared them with the broadcast schedule and found a backup job running during the busiest hour.
evidence.mark: monitored a community media server during live broadcasts

evidence.quote: I wrote a runbook for the person on duty when the media server stopped responding. It lists the checks in order and says when to call the supplier.
I wrote automated browser tests for a sports club membership service. The tests cover joining, changing an address and cancelling a booking.

I collected the results from several test runs and grouped failures by screen and browser. Most came from the same date field on small screens. I compared the failed cases, wrote a clear issue and checked the change after it was released.
evidence.mark: collected the results from several test runs and grouped failures by screen and browser

evidence.quote: I wrote SQL queries to compare the old totals with the new database. The finance team could trace every total back to an order.
I combined monthly order files into a PostgreSQL database for a small distributor. The files used different customer codes, so I made a mapping table and checked duplicates before importing anything.
evidence.mark: combined monthly order files into a PostgreSQL database

evidence.quote: I drew a data model showing customers, orders and returns and explained it to the finance team. I wrote the import checks next to the diagram, including how to handle a missing identifier.
evidence.mark: drew a data model showing customers, orders and returns

evidence.quote: I built a booking form for our community workshop using JavaScript and a small web server. I first drew the screens with the volunteers, then made a working prototype they could try on their phones.
I first drew the screens with the volunteers, then made a working prototype they could try on their phones. We changed the form after watching where people got stuck.
We changed the form after watching where people got stuck. The workshop now uses it for weekly sessions.

Our booking page sometimes recorded the same booking twice. I reproduced the problem, traced the request logs and found a missing check when a phone retried a slow request. I fixed the check and wrote test cases for repeated requests and missing fields.
evidence.mark: reproduced the problem, traced the request logs and found a missing check when a phone retried a slow request. I fixed the check

evidence.quote: I built a spreadsheet that logged everything we threw away, by day and by reason. I compared the totals each week and found that most waste came from sandwiches prepared after lunch.

I built a spreadsheet that logged everything we threw away, by day and by reason. I compared the totals each week and found that most waste came from sandwiches prepared after lunch. I changed the preparation quantities and checked the following weeks.
evidence.mark: compared the totals each week and found that most waste came from sandwiches prepared after lunch

evidence.quote: I organised stock checks and showed six new colleagues how to update the ordering sheet. I wrote a one-page guide with examples of the mistakes we had made.

I organised stock checks and showed six new colleagues how to update the ordering sheet. I wrote a one-page guide with examples of the mistakes we had made. Each person tried a practice order while I watched.
evidence.mark: showed six new colleagues how to update the ordering sheet

evidence.quote: I collected brake and battery measurements in a bicycle repair workshop. I labelled each bike, recorded the tool settings and repeated unusual readings before entering them in the sheet.

I compared the results from repeated battery tests and plotted the readings by temperature. One test stand gave consistently lower readings, so I swapped the measuring leads and repeated the test. The difference followed the damaged lead.
evidence.mark: compared the results from repeated battery tests and plotted the readings by temperature

evidence.quote: I built a spreadsheet listing each item, its return date and its condition, then checked it against the shelf every Friday. I used formulas to flag overdue returns and low stock.
I kept the stock records at an equipment rental desk. I built a spreadsheet listing each item, its return date and its condition, then checked it against the shelf every Friday.
I handled customer questions when a rented tool stopped working. I asked what had happened, checked the return notes and agreed a replacement with the supervisor.
I taught two new colleagues how to check returns and update the stock sheet. We practised with damaged items and missing parts before their first busy shift.
evidence.mark: taught two new colleagues how to check returns and update the stock sheet
